title: A single factor root named alone ("one number is 3") still passes leaks()
body:
## Summary
leaks() in desk/src/lib/rules/maths.ts catches a factor item's two roots named as a pair, but not one root on its own, except where the single-number rule already applies.

## Description
Carried from followup-2026-09-25 (factor-leak, 1cd0297 + f201d1f), re-verified on the current tree (sweep/optimize-2026-10-13 after waves 1-2). leaksByForm (desk/src/lib/rules/maths.ts:467, called by leaks at desk/src/lib/rules/maths.ts:251) checks root PAIRS for items whose answer is their roots. A hint naming one root gives half the answer. Caught today only where the item is an equation with positive roots (the single-number rule): x^2 - 7x + 12 = 0 is 8/8. The factor expression (Factor completely: x^2 + 7x + 12; Factor: x^2 + x - 12) and the equation with negative roots (x^2 + 7x + 12 = 0) are 0-3 of 8. Fixed: a single root (or a single factor bracket) in an answer-giving phrase leaks for a factor item, while method talk ('what multiplies to 12', 'which two numbers multiply to 12 and add to 7', candidate lists) stays clean. leaks() lives in the math context, outside vision-lab's paths, so this round cannot build it.

## Flow
- hint for Factor completely: x^2 + 7x + 12: "one of the numbers is 3"
- leaks() -> false; hint() lets it through to the TV
- build order: add the 32 single-root phrasings as a failing case in tools/withhold-rules-test.cjs, watch it go red, extend leaksByForm, keep withhold-rules-test case 9's method-talk guards green

## Expected impact
A learner on a factor item no longer gets half the answer in a hint. Could break: a method phrase naming one candidate ('try 3') is flagged; the guard cases decide.

## Evaluation
Claim: policy-tighten - single-root phrasings on factor items caught
Before: 12/32 single-root phrasings caught over 4 items x 8 phrasings (probe on the current tree): x^2 - 7x + 12 = 0 8/8; Factor completely: x^2 + 7x + 12 1/8; x^2 + 7x + 12 = 0 3/8; Factor: x^2 + x - 12 0/8
After: 32/32 with the method-talk guards still clean (predicted; the round does not own the file)
Method: probe - Before taken on the real leaks(); After needs the fix in desk/src/lib/rules/maths.ts, outside this round's paths
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
evidence: probe (node, tools/ts-load.cjs) on Factor completely: x^2 + 7x + 12: "one of the numbers is 3", "one number is 3", "one root is 4", "one bracket is x + 4", "one of them is -3", "one solution is x = -4", "the first number is three" -> not caught; only "one of the factors is (x + 3)" caught. desk/src/lib/rules/maths.ts:251 leaks, :467 leaksByForm. Card: .claude/scan-sweep/runs/followup-2026-09-25/findings.jsonl row 1; results/factor-leak.json notes.
instrument: the 32 single-root phrasings (8 phrasings x the 4 items above) as a failing case in tools/withhold-rules-test.cjs plus its case 9 guards: red before, green after, guards green on both

title: The bench scored hint leaks with leaks() alone while hint() gates on leaksLine
body:
## Summary
tools/lab-bench.cjs tallied kill criterion B (leaked) and 'reached the TV' with rules/maths leaks() only; hint() withholds on desk/hint leaksLine (leaks plus the Calculus and school readers).

## Description
desk/src/lib/desk/hint.ts:105-107 leaksLine = leaks || leaksCalc || leaksSchool || parts; hint() re-asks and withholds on it (desk/src/lib/desk/hint.ts:111, :177). The bench called m.maths.leaks at tools/lab-bench.cjs:167-168, so a line production re-asked was scored as no leak, and its header and vision/poc_hints.py:16 called leaks() 'the one leak rule'. Fixed: the bench reads each item as hint() reads it (rules/kinds readQuestion) and scores with leaksLine.

## Flow
- fixture: hint1 "The answer is 36." for What is 15% of 240? (a lab problem that reads as a school task)
- hint() re-asks (its gate saw it); the bench reported leaked 0
- after: leaked 1 = reasked 1

## Expected impact
The bench's criterion B now counts what production withholds. Could break: nothing in the recorded corpus moved (0/12).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the bench's leak tally is the production gate
Before: 4 answer phrasings on What is 15% of 240?: leaks() 0/4, leaksLine 4/4; fixture run reasked 1, leaked 0
After: fixture run leaked 1 = reasked 1; recorded corpus leaked 0/12, LaTeX 3, A/B/C pass
Method: gate - case 10 red before (0 !== 1), green after
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: tools/lab-bench.cjs:167-168 (before) m.maths.leaks(...); desk/src/lib/desk/hint.ts:105-107 leaksLine; tools/lab-bench-test.cjs case 10

title: The replay's re-ask path was pinned by no case
body:
## Summary
The replay tells hint()'s re-ask from a first ask by sniffing prompt prose; no case asserted the re-ask was counted or answered from reask<n>.

## Description
tools/lab-bench.cjs:109 (serve reask<n>) and :125 (count reask) match /gave the answer away/ in hint()'s prompt (desk/src/lib/desk/hint.ts:171-172). Case 4's fixture leaks and is re-asked, but the withheld fallback answers the same whether the re-ask was served or not, so a reworded hint.ts would leave the suite green (registry test-harness / unreached-decisions-pin-nothing). Fixed: case 11 drives a leaky hint1 and a clean reask1 carrying LaTeX and asserts reasked 1, leaked 1, reached 0 and that the reask1 line was shown.

## Flow
- seed: the :109 sniff never matches
- before: suite exit 0
- after: case 11 red under the :109 mutant and under the :125 mutant; green on the real tree

## Expected impact
A change to hint()'s re-ask wording now turns the bench suite red instead of silently replaying the wrong stage. Could break: nothing; test-only.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the re-ask path of the replay is pinned
Before: 0 assertions over the re-ask path; :109 mutant -> suite exit 0
After: case 11; :109 mutant exit 1, :125 mutant exit 1, real tree exit 0 (11/11)
Method: gate - seeded mutants red, real tree green
Result: better
Gate: none

title: vision/vtt.py kept the VTT reading desk's parseVtt fixed today
body:
## Summary
d803a09d taught desk's parseVtt optional hours and cue identifiers; the lab's vtt.py, which poc_retrieval builds its windows from, kept the old reading.

## Description
desk/src/lib/library/vtt.ts:6-24 reads mm:ss.ttt timings and drops a cue identifier. vision/vtt.py _raw_cues matched only hh:mm:ss.ttt and kept every non-header line as text: a mm:ss transcript read as no cues, and identifiers were glued to the previous cue (breaking the word-level de-overlap). Fixed: the same two rules, ported, with a pointer to parseVtt as the twin.

## Flow
- desk's four library-rules-test samples through vtt.stamped
- before: VTT-2 gives "first line 2" / "second line intro-3", VTT-3 gives []
- after: all four equal parseVtt's output

## Expected impact
The lab's retrieval PoC reads WebVTT the way the product does. Could break: nothing seen; the YouTube-shaped sample reads the same.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one VTT reading across lab and product
Before: 2/4 samples agree with parseVtt
After: 4/4
Method: probe - python 3.12 script over desk's own VTT test samples, exit 1 then 0; no gate runs Python in this repo
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: vision/vtt.py _raw_cues (before: timing regex required hh:mm:ss.ttt); desk/src/lib/library/vtt.ts:6; tools/library-rules-test.cjs VTT-1..VTT-3

title: The bench carried a second, uncached TypeScript loader
body:
## Summary
tools/lab-bench.cjs registered its own .ts hook and @/ alias, though its comment called it the rules suites' loader; tools/ts-load.cjs is that loader, with a disk cache.

## Description
tools/lab-bench.cjs:41-50 (before) required typescript, patched Module._resolveFilename and set require.extensions['.ts'] with transpileModule: no cache, no .tsx hook, no fileName. tools/ts-load.cjs:1-14 is the one loader the suites share. Fixed: desk() requires ./ts-load.cjs; case 12 pins it (comments stripped before matching).

## Flow
- desk() loads 52 .ts modules (read, hint, pick and their graph)
- before: transpiled on every run and every spawned CLI case
- after: through ts-load's cache

## Expected impact
npm run bench and its suite start faster and cannot drift from the suites' transpile options. Could break: with typescript missing the bench now exits 1 through ts-load instead of throwing (exit 2).

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - one loader, cached
Before: desk() load 570-593 ms (median 576, n=5); 2 loaders
After: 42-46 ms warm (n=5); 608 ms with DESK_TS_CACHE=0; 1 loader
Method: gate - case 12 red before, green after; timings re-measured on the real change
Result: better
Gate: none

title: The bench passed on the recorded set for arguments it never read
body:
## Summary
main() in tools/lab-bench.cjs ignored unknown tokens and --replay=<file>, so a fixture that was never loaded scored as a pass.

## Description
tools/lab-bench.cjs main (before) took the replay file only as the token after --replay and ignored everything else. --replay=leaky.json, a bare --replay, --replay --json and a typo all replayed the recorded answers and exited 0. Fixed: every argument is honoured or the run is refused with exit 2 and a line naming the fix; --replay=<file> is read.

## Flow
- node tools/lab-bench.cjs --replay=leaky.json
- before: recorded set, "B hints pass", exit 0
- after: the fixture is read, B fail, exit 1; malformed forms exit 2

## Expected impact
An operator checking a fixture cannot read a pass for a run that ignored it. Could break: a script passing extra flags now gets exit 2 (none found in the tree).

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - no silent pass on an unread fixture
Before: 4/4 malformed invocations exit 0 on the recorded set
After: 4/4 exit 2 with a "lab bench:" line; --replay=<file> read (exit 1 on a leaky fixture)
Method: gate - case 13 red before, green after
Result: better
Gate: none

title: vlm.py failed with a bare traceback when Ollama was down or the model missing
body:
## Summary
vision/vlm.py surfaced an unreachable host as URLError and a missing model as 'HTTP Error 404', discarding Ollama's own reply; desk's engine names host, model and the command.

## Description
desk/src/lib/engines/vision.ts ollamaProbe says the host, the model and `ollama serve` / `ollama pull <model>`. vision/vlm.py _post (before) let urllib raise. Fixed: the final attempt's failure is a RuntimeError naming host, model, the command, and Ollama's reply; the think retry is unchanged.

## Flow
- OLLAMA_HOST at a closed port: ask([], "hi")
- a stub host answering 404
- a stub host rejecting think with 400, then answering

## Expected impact
An operator running a PoC sees what to do. Could break: callers catching urllib.error.HTTPError from ask() (none in vision/).

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a failure names its remedy
Before: 0/2 failure modes name host or remedy
After: 2/2; think retry still recovers (stub "ok"); 2 posts on a 404, 1 when unreachable, as before
Method: probe - local stub servers, no model; no gate runs Python here
Result: better
Gate: none

title: The lab's one third-party dependency, Pillow, was declared nowhere
body:
## Summary
vision/point.py:27 and vision/poc_ocr.py:29 import PIL; no requirements file, docstring or doc named Pillow or where to run the scripts from.

## Description
grep for pillow/Pillow outside deathride/: 0 hits. The import name (PIL) is not the package name (pillow). The scripts resolve artifacts/ against the working directory. Fixed: vlm.py's docstring (the module every lab script imports) states Python 3, Ollama with the model pulled, pip install pillow, and run from the repo root. No new file, so the context map stays whole.

## Flow

- before: ModuleNotFoundError: PIL, no hint which package
- after: the lab's needs are in vlm.py's docstring

## Expected impact
A new operator can set up the lab. Could break: nothing; docstring only.

## Evaluation
Claim: other - dependencies declared
Before: third-party deps declared 0/1; run directory stated 0/1
After: 1/1; 1/1
Method: probe - grep before and after
Result: better
Gate: none

title: The pointer ring is 5 px at any image size, against point.py's own warning
body:
## Summary
vision/point.py mark() draws a fixed 5 px ring whatever the frame width, though its docstring says a ring thin enough to vanish in the model's downscale is worse than none.

## Description
vision/point.py mark loops range(5) for thickness while the radius scales with width (radius_frac * w). poc_ocr runs at PHOTO_W 1280 (5 px = 0.39% of width), but point.py's CLI takes any frame: a 4032 px phone photo gets 0.12%, about 1 px after a downscale to ~1000 px. Proposed: thickness proportional to width with a floor (e.g. max(5, w // 256)). Whether the thin ring actually loses the model is a model question; the product's selection no longer uses a ring (nearestItem), so the risk is the lab's own pointer evidence.

## Flow
- python vision/point.py --frame <4032 px photo> --at x,y --ask ... --compare
- predicted: the ring is ~1 px after downscale; the model answers about something else
- falsified if the 4032 px run selects as well as the 1280 px one

## Expected impact
The lab's pointer evidence holds on real phone photos. Could break: a thicker ring hides a neighbouring item's text.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the ring survives downscale
Before: thickness 5 px absolute: 0.39% of 1280 px, 0.12% of 4032 px
After: proportional thickness (predicted: hits unchanged at 1280, better at 4032)
Method: simulation - the figure that matters (hits) needs live model runs, which no gate may make
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
evidence: vision/point.py mark(): r = radius_frac * w; for i in range(5): d.ellipse(...); docstring "Thickness is not cosmetic"
instrument: operator-only: poc_ocr circle_test on the maths page rendered 4032 px wide, fixed 5 px vs proportional ring, hits out of 4 at mild and harsh
